title: arXiv Physics Daily — 2026-10-28: measurements across nuclear, quantum, and astrophysical physics
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart, so this is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not a popularity list; citation evidence is limited because all nine selected papers had zero Semantic Scholar citations at the snapshot.

sections.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
sections.abstract: The authors measure the beta decay of neutron-rich potassium-54 and report that state-of-the-art calculations including two-body weak currents reproduce the measured Gamow–Teller strength.
sections.claimed_result: At FRIB, the authors report a dominant transition to a neutron-unbound state near 6.2 MeV and a Gamow–Teller strength B(GT)=0.26(+0.08/−0.04); they say calculations with two-body currents reproduce the measurement, supporting an important role for those currents in neutron-rich nuclei.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; FRIB radioactive-ion-beam beta-decay measurement compared with VS-IMSRG and shell-model calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The inference is anchored in one isotope and depends on the decay-state spin assignment; raw FRIB data are available from the authors on request, while calculation results are public.

sections.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of φ, K⁰S, and Λ elliptic flow
sections.abstract: The ALICE Collaboration reports the first identified-hadron elliptic-flow measurements in oxygen–oxygen collisions at √sNN=5.36 TeV, finding patterns consistent with collective expansion and quark recombination.
sections.claimed_result: ALICE measures v₂ for φ, K⁰S, and Λ/anti-Λ; above 3 GeV/c, Λ has larger v₂ than the mesons at 10σ significance, while φ follows K⁰S. The authors interpret this as support for partonic collectivity and quark recombination in a light-ion system.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; identified-particle flow analysis of ALICE O–O collision data at 5.36 TeV.
sections.unique_caveat: The flow pattern is evidence consistent with a collectively flowing partonic medium, not by itself a unique demonstration of QGP formation; interpretation depends on flow extraction and competing hadronization explanations.

sections.title: Coulomb Crystallization in Free Electron Beams
sections.abstract: Transmission-electron-microscope measurements and many-body modelling indicate transient Coulomb ordering in freely propagating few-electron pulses, with the authors predicting ways to extend it to larger and continuous beams.
sections.claimed_result: Number-resolved energy correlations in photoemitted pulses of up to nine electrons are consistent with transient ordering; the authors attribute confinement of inner electrons to a self-induced potential from the leading and trailing particles.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; transmission electron microscopy, many-body simulations, and a one-dimensional statistical-mechanical model.
sections.unique_caveat: The measured ordering is transient and demonstrated in few-electron pulses; larger-particle and continuous-beam crystallization are predictions requiring additional transverse guiding, not experimental demonstrations here.

sections.title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
sections.abstract: The authors report tunable loss of electron diffraction coherence near a metal surface, which they interpret as experimental evidence for quantum-Brownian-motion-driven electron–metal decoherence.
sections.claimed_result: Electron diffraction fringes lose visibility in a gold-plated microchannel, and the visibility changes continuously with channel tilt in quantitative agreement with the authors’ decoherence model.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; electron diffraction with a thermionic electron beam and a gold-plated microchannel.
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis models the interaction as a single bounce; surface roughness, electron loss, and the subset of electrons that reach the detector limit how broadly the measured decoherence can be generalized.

sections.title: Detection of star formation in a near-pristine pocket of the Universe
sections.abstract: Keck/KCWI observations reveal two Lyα-emitting, star-forming sources in the environment of a chemically near-pristine damped Lyα absorber at redshift 3.078.
sections.claimed_result: The authors detect two Lyα sources at projected separations of 66 and 137 physical kpc from a DLA with [Fe/H] < −3.66, and set 3σ upper limits on associated He II emission.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; Keck/KCWI integral-field spectroscopy of a quasar sightline and its surrounding field.
sections.unique_caveat: The sources are in the DLA environment, not proven to be the absorber’s host; the data do not determine their metallicities, and the authors call for rest-frame optical follow-up.

sections.title: Periodic radio emission from a rapidly rotating T8 ultracool dwarf
sections.abstract: ASKAP and MeerKAT observations reveal periodic radio bursts from the T8 brown dwarf WISE J1517+05 with a 1.149±0.002-hour period, which the authors attribute to auroral electron-cyclotron maser emission.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report highly variable, bright, broadband bursts with a stable 1.149-hour period and low, variable circular polarization; they infer a rapidly rotating, magnetized ultracool dwarf.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; radio observations with ASKAP and MeerKAT, supplemented by other radio data described in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: This is one object; its polarization reversal remains unexplained, and the inferred magnetic geometry assumes a dipole field with emission from one active field line.

sections.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-Λ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
sections.abstract: ALICE reports the first antideuteron–net-Λ number-correlation measurement in Pb–Pb collisions and finds it, along with a net-Λ cumulant, consistent with a statistical-hadronization model.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that the antideuteron–net-Λ correlation and normalized second-order net-Λ cumulant agree with Thermal-FIST’s statistical-hadronization implementation, supporting a nucleosynthesis origin for the previously observed antideuteron–antiproton correlation.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; event-by-event particle-number correlations in ALICE Pb–Pb data, compared with the Thermal-FIST model.
sections.unique_caveat: Agreement with one statistical-hadronization implementation is not a unique proof of the production mechanism; this is a distinct observable from the O–O flow result, not an independent confirmation of it.

sections.title: ASKAP Discovery of a Giant Odd Radio Circle at z=0.15
sections.abstract: ASKAP 856-MHz continuum data reveal a 0.63-Mpc odd radio circle around the brightest cluster galaxy of Abell 3639, among the largest single ORCs reported by the authors.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report ORC J1928−5056 at z=0.1507, with 73 mJy integrated flux after subtracting the radio nucleus, and discuss possible formation scenarios.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; 856-MHz ASKAP FLASH continuum imaging, with higher-frequency radio and optical context for the host.
sections.unique_caveat: The physical origin is unresolved and the claim is based on one source; follow-up spectral and polarization measurements are needed to distinguish formation models.

sections.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
sections.abstract: The authors forecast that simulated LISA extreme-mass-ratio-inspiral signals could constrain ultralight-dark-matter particle masses through wave-dependent interactions with a dense dark-matter spike.
sections.claimed_result: For simulated LISA signals from low-mass massive black holes, the authors forecast order-of-magnitude constraints on ultralight-dark-matter masses between 10⁻¹⁴ and 10⁻¹¹ eV.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; relativistic inspiral waveform modelling and parameter inference on simulated LISA signals.
sections.unique_caveat: The forecast requires sufficiently dense dark-matter spikes and depends on the assumed spike profile and environmental accretion and dynamical-friction model; it is not a detection or a measurement with LISA data.
